subject: Heliosphere: latency spike & error-rate surge — exec war-room activation
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@heliosphere.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@heliosphere.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Heliosphere production: sudden latency + 5xx increase

Laura —

We started seeing a severe increase in end-to-end latency across our customer-facing routes around 07:50 PT and an accompanying spike in 5xx errors (auth and generate endpoints). Traffic patterns are otherwise normal; tokens per request average is unchanged. Impact: about 18% of requests are timing out or returning 5xx, customers are reporting slow UI responses.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity/serving regression on your side or something in our front-end retries? We need an exec-level update for our leadership in 2 hours. Happy to hop in a call if that speeds things up.

Attachments: telemetry_snapshot_heliosphere_07150.png (screenshot from our APM)

Sofia Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering
Heliosphere AI
sramos@heliosphere.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@heliosphere.ai>, Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@heliosphere.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Heliosphere production: sudden latency + 5xx increase

Team — activating an exec war-room for Heliosphere. This has high customer and C-level visibility; treat as P0.

Immediate asks:
- David: pull GPU-level telemetry (util, memory, queue length) and model-side error logs for the past 90 minutes. Include any config rollouts we did in the last 24 hours.
- Karthik: check routing policies and autoscale decisions for the Heliosphere tenant; can we spin up dedicated capacity in us-west-2 for a hot-fix window?
- Neha: prep a short customer-facing statement and a cadence (every 30m) for status updates.

I'll join the incident bridge and loop in the head of Sales if we need credit/contract exceptions.

War-room bridge: https://redwood.zoom.us/j/987654321
Incident board: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2027-558

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@heliosphere.ai>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@heliosphere.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Heliosphere production: sudden latency + 5xx increase

On the bridge — initial telemetry snapshot attached (telemetry_snapshot_20271102.png). Top-level findings so far:

- GPU utilization across the Heliosphere pool jumped to 98% between 07:48–08:10 PT; queuing increased on the router layer.
- Error breakdown: ~65% of 5xx are originating from the model runtime (kv cache misses -> memory pressure) and ~35% are upstream auth gateway timeouts.
- No config rollouts show in the rollout history for the Heliosphere tenant in the last 24 hours.
- We observed a small bump in concurrent short-lived spike traffic from a single consumer key (~3x baseline for ~4 minutes) which appears to have triggered queue growth.

Short mitigation we executed at 11:10 PT:
- Throttled the noisy API key to baseline and temporarily routed ~20% of Heliosphere traffic to the warm fallback model variant (quantized) to relieve pressure.
- Cleared a stale KV cache shard on two nodes.

Next steps (in-progress):
- Karthik to schedule an immediate burst for Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 for 2 hours.
- Preparing a runbook patch to address the cache shard clearing logic (attached: runbook_patch_v1.diff).

Attaching: telemetry_snapshot_20271102.png, runbook_patch_v1.diff

-David
David Kim
Director, Runtime & Reliability
redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, david.kim@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@heliosphere.ai>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@heliosphere.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Heliosphere production: sudden latency + 5xx increase

Quick update from ops — capacity and routing actions:

- Reserved two additional Dedicated pods in us-west-2 and pushed traffic routing changes; should provide ~35% additional headroom within 3–5 minutes.
- Opened a temporary exception to autoscale thresholds for Heliosphere to allow faster spin-up during this surge window.
- Recommended config change: enable aggressive KV prefetch for the next 4 hours for Heliosphere’s most common prefixes (I can roll this in a short maintenance window).

I will monitor for 30m and confirm whether the dedicated nodes are absorbing the load. If error-rate continues, propose short-term plan B: route heavy customers to a quantized variant plus increase request-timeout to reduce client-side retries.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <s.ramos@heliosphere.ai>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@heliosphere.ai>, procurement@heliosphere.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Heliosphere incident update — stabilization and next steps

Sofia / Tom —

Summary (high level):
- Timeline: spike started ~07:48 PT on 2027-11-02; mitigations applied the same day (throttle, warm-fallback routing, cache shard clears, extra Dedicated pods) and achieved stabilization within ~4 hours.
- Impact: transient increase in 5xx and latency affecting ~18% of requests at peak. We routed ~20% of production traffic to a quantized fallback to reduce pressure and spun up dedicated capacity to restore headroom.
- Current state: service is stable; 5xx and latency back within SLOs for the last 22 hours. We continue to monitor with enhanced telemetry.

What we did for Heliosphere:
- Immediate: throttled noisy key, cleared cache shards, routed traffic to fallback model variant.
- Capacity: burst-provisioned dedicated nodes in us-west-2 and opened autoscale exception.
- Long-term: engineering is patching the KV shard clearing logic (runbook_patch_v1.diff attached) and we are evaluating a segmented autoscale profile for tenants with bursty traffic patterns.

Customer asks / open items:
- Procurement: we will likely need a temporary SLA exception & a short-term Reserved Capacity add-on for November to ensure predictability during the seasonal campaign. Attached: sla_exception_request_heliosphere.pdf for procurement review.
- Action: Laura to schedule a post-incident review (PIER) with Heliosphere for next week; David to present telemetry and Karthik to present the runtime fixes.

Proposed next steps:
- PR 1: Post-incident review on Mon 2027-11-08 10:00 PT (invite to follow).
- PR 2: Apply runbook_patch_v1 in canary on 2027-11-05; monitor 48h.
- PR 3: Sales/Account to discuss temporary reserved capacity quote and SLA exception (procurement@heliosphere.ai is looped).

Thanks for rapid coordination — we’ll continue updates in the incident board and I’ll circulate the post-incident write-up once the runbook patch completes verification.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123
